slides.title: How many new clothes does the average Australian buy in a year?
slides.notes: Ask the question. Students vote with a hand held up: closed fist = fewer than 10, one finger = about 10, two fingers = about 20, and so on; five fingers = 50 or more. Count to three and everyone shows at once. Look around the room, then click for the reveal.

slides.section: Sources: Seamless (2024), The Australia Institute, Australian Fashion Council.
slides.title: 55 new items of clothing
slides.notes: Reveal 55. Pause. "Who guessed close?" Give a cheer for the nearest. That is more than one new item a week. 1.51 billion new items are sold or imported into Australia every year.

slides.title: What goes into one T-shirt?
slides.notes:
Hold up a T-shirt if you have one. "Before you wear it, look at where its carbon comes from." Fibre production 15%, yarn preparation 28%, fabric preparation about 12%, dyeing and finishing 36%, everything else about 9% (sewing, transport, end of life). Then the tag: many items are worn only about 7 times (Baptist World Aid Ethical Fashion Report).

Click for where it all ends up.

slides.title: Circular fashion: keep clothes in use
slides.notes:
Bridge from the problem to what we do. Australia sells 1.51 billion new clothing items every year, 55 new items per person, and about 220,000 tonnes of clothing end up in landfill. The problem is not that we lack materials. It is that we have not designed systems capable of keeping materials in productive use.

The circular order, left to right:
- Redesign: create products and systems that make circularity economically and practically viable.
- Reduce: buy fewer new materials and products.
- Repair: restore their usefulness.
- Reuse: extend the life of existing products.
- Repurpose: find new applications for existing materials.
- Recycle, then landfill last.

Mixed materials are hard to recycle because they are joined together and hard to separate. Unstitch sits on reuse and repurpose: the tiles come apart so they can be used again, and the system is a redesign of how fabric products are made.

Timing: about 30 seconds.

slides.title: Unstitch: tex-tiles without sewing or stitching
slides.notes: Lead on from landfill and the ladder. Introduce the tiles: hold up a real tile or the kit, and connect and disconnect it (no sewing, no stitching). The collage shows what people have made with the same tiles. Name four ideas: modularity (tiles combine into larger structures), reversibility (connections can be undone without adhesives or damage), adaptability (the same tiles can be rearranged into different outcomes) and material efficiency (existing components are reused and reconfigured). The fifth idea, thinking by making, comes on the challenge slide.

slides.title: Who we are
slides.notes: Keep it short and personal: how you started, why fabric, what you hope they feel today. Swap in your photography. The speech bubble reads "I am [name]": replace [name] with your own, or duplicate the mascot and bubble for each team member.

slides.title: The challenge
slides.notes: Read the challenge aloud, then introduce thinking by making: we rethink, reuse and recreate by building, not only discussing. Rethink. Reuse. Recreate. Next: who is on the team.

slides.title: Meet your design team: Designer
slides.notes: Designer: leads the idea exploration so the team builds something with a clear user and purpose.

slides.title: Meet your design team: Material Keeper
slides.notes: Material Keeper: looks after the tiles, making sure they are in good condition and can be reused as much as possible.

slides.title: Meet your design team: Builder
slides.notes: Builder: builds the design and makes sure it holds together and is stable.

slides.title: Meet your design team: Tech Wizard
slides.notes: Tech Wizard: tries configurations in the playground and brings the best ideas to the team.

slides.title: Meet your design team: Storyteller
slides.notes: Storyteller: keeps track of decisions, includes everyone and prepares the show and tell.

slides.title: What is in your kit
slides.notes: Go through the kit: 24 tiles, the virtual playground, five role cards (one each) and the digital brief on their device. The QR code on the Begin the challenge slide opens the brief.

slides.title: Your four constraints
slides.notes: These are the four things your design must do. Read them out. The fourth is time: 20 minutes to build and test. Point out the timer in the corner of the projector (it is part of the hub view).

slides.title: The design loop and the clock
slides.notes:
Read left to right. 5 minutes for the brief. 15 minutes to explore and build. A ding (the bell). 5 minutes to test and refine. A ding. 5 minutes to share: show and tell. Last 10 minutes: unbuild and reflect. That is 40 minutes after the 5-minute welcome. The loop shows it all returning to the start: circular design, nothing is thrown away.

Suggested dings: after 5: "Brief done: start exploring." After 20: "Time to test. Does it do what you said? Try the virtual playground." After 25: "Wrap up. Show and tell time."

Hand out the kit now. The timer is in the corner of the projector view.

slides.title: Begin the challenge
slides.notes:
Hand out the kits. Read the challenge and the four constraints once (the fourth is time). Remind teams of the five roles.

The QR code opens the workshop page for students (the Participants page). If a phone can't scan it, they can type the code shown under it.

The countdown is in the top-right corner and moves on to Explore & build on this slide. Press Start if it is not already running, and say "Go!".

slides.title: Want to share? Show your bid card
slides.notes:
"If your team wants to present, the Storyteller holds up the bid card." Choose 2 to 3 teams. One minute each, covering: our idea, our innovation, our discovery. Keep it moving; applaud each team.

Confirm the show and tell duration for your session (5 minutes in total).

slides.title: Close the loop
slides.notes:
Close the loop. Click for the UNBUILD and REFLECT steps.

UNBUILD (the Material Keeper leads): 1 dismantle your design, 2 pack and wrap up the tiles, 3 return the kit.

slides.title: Unbuild and reflect
slides.notes:
Two parts.

UNBUILD (the Material Keeper leads): 1 dismantle your design, 2 pack and wrap up the tiles, 3 return the kit.

REFLECT: students scan the upper QR code to give feedback on the website (the screenshot shows the form). Teachers scan the lower QR code for the teacher feedback form. If a phone can't scan, open the workshop page and scroll to "How was today?". Your own feedback form is at the bottom of the Facilitator tab here.

Reflection prompts if time allows: What would you rethink? What could you reuse? What would you recreate next time?

slides.title: Thank you!
slides.notes: Thank the students and the school. The key message to leave them with is one word: rethink. "What will you rethink next?" Hand back to the teacher.
